chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Saif ibn Umayrah, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said:
I heard Salman saying: Eat from what the dog held (and did not swallow), even if it ate two-thirds of it.

key_terms.أَمْسَكَ: Held or gripped (referring to the dog holding the prey)
key_terms.سَلْمَانُ: Salman (al-Farsi), a prominent companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Is meat permissible to eat if a dog has caught it and eaten part of it?
ai.summary: This narration from Salman al-Farsi, transmitted via the reliable chain of Aban ibn Taghlib, clarifies the principle of *istihlak* (consumption) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between partial consumption and total destruction of the prey. It establishes that as long as the dog has not fully swallowed or digested the meat, the remaining portion retains its original state of purity (*tahir*) and is permissible to consume, even if a majority like two-thirds has been eaten. This ruling is foundational in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for determining the validity of game caught by hunting dogs.
